scene.bubble: The new neighbours arrive today! Let's learn to describe people — without pointing, Mateo!
scene.intro: The new neighbours arrive today, so Erik and Sofía practise describing people. He has got short dark hair and glasses. She has got long hair and green eyes. The grandfather has got a white beard and he is quite old; the baby is very young. Nobody is 'normal' — everybody is different. Describe someone in your class and let your friends guess who it is!

activities.title: Grammar · The girl who is riding a bike
activities.instructions: Read the sentences. Then choose the right word.

data.title: One sentence, not two
data.intro: Two short sentences about the same person? Join them with who. For a thing use which, for a place use where. In the Speaking test this is how you say which person you mean.
data.can: I can join two sentences with who, which and where to say exactly which person, thing or place I mean.

examples.text: Vicky is the girl who is riding a bike.
This person helps people who aren’t well.
My friend is the boy who has got curly hair and a green shirt.
That’s the shop which has the best bread, next to the park where we play.

rules: who for people · which for things and animals · where for places.
The joining word comes straight after the person or thing: the girl who…, not the girl she…
Do not say the person twice: never the girl who she is riding a bike.

items.sentence: Sofia is the girl ___ has got long black hair.
That is the bike ___ my grandma gave me.
This is the park ___ we play football on Saturdays.
A doctor is a person ___ helps you when you are ill.

options: The boy who he is running.
